description: Golden reference cases validating tropical Sun longitude against independently published equinox/solstice UTC instants. At an equinox the Sun's tropical ecliptic longitude is exactly 0 deg (March) or 180 deg (September); at a solstice it is exactly 90 deg (June) or 270 deg (December) -- by definition, independent of any astrology software.
source: Published UTC times for the 2024 equinoxes/solstices, cross-referenced across timeanddate.com, CBS News, and thesuntoday.org (retrieved via web search during Phase 4 implementation, 2026-09).
methodology: For each case, compute tropical (zodiac=tropical, ayanamsa=null) Sun longitude at the given UTC instant and assert it equals the expected value within tolerance_degrees.

cases.name: 2024 March equinox
cases.note: 0/360 boundary -- longitude may report as ~359.999 or ~0.001
